title: Vector Physics Numerical Problems — Page 60 (Q13–Q17)
notes:
**Q13. One of the rectangular components of a vector of 100 units is 50 units. Find the other component.**

**Answer:** $50\sqrt{3}$ units

**Solution:** Using the rectangular component relationship: $R^2 = R_x^2 + R_y^2$. Therefore, $100^2 = 50^2 + R_y^2 \Rightarrow 10000 = 2500 + R_y^2 \Rightarrow R_y^2 = 7500 \Rightarrow R_y = \sqrt{7500} = 50\sqrt{3}$ units.

**Q14. A particle has a displacement of 8m. If one of its rectangular components is 4m, what is the other rectangular component?**

**Answer:** 6.92 m

**Solution:** Using $R^2 = R_x^2 + R_y^2$: $8^2 = 4^2 + R_y^2 \Rightarrow 64 = 16 + R_y^2 \Rightarrow R_y^2 = 48 \Rightarrow R_y = \sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3} \approx 6.928$ m.

**Q15. A force of 20N is inclined at 30° to the X-axis. Calculate its X and Y components.**

**Answer:** $10\sqrt{3}$ N, 10N

**Solution:** X-component: $F_x = F \cdot \cos(30°) = 20 \cdot (\sqrt{3}/2) = 10\sqrt{3}$ N. Y-component: $F_y = F \cdot \sin(30°) = 20 \times 0.5 = 10$N.

**Q16. A vector $F = i + 2j - 3k$ is given. What is the magnitude of the y-component of the vector?**

**Answer:** 2

**Solution:** The y-component of a vector expressed in standard orthogonal base notation is simply the scalar coefficient of the unit vector j, which is 2.

**Q17. The x-component of a vector is -10 unit and its y-component is +3 unit. Find out the magnitude and direction of the vector.**

**Answer:** 10.4 units, 17° above negative x-axis

**Solution:** Magnitude $= \sqrt{(-10)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{100 + 9} = \sqrt{109} \approx 10.44$ units. Direction angle with the negative x-axis: $\tan(\theta) = |R_y| / |R_x| = 3 / 10 = 0.3 \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.3) \approx 16.7°$ (rounded to 17° above the negative x-axis).
